key_insight: A two-level machine-learning workflow can efficiently map phase stability across complex hybrid perovskite alloy compositions, revealing that Sn-based alloys are less stable than Pb-based ones.
engineering_relevance: The stability maps provide design rules for selecting alloy compositions that maximize thermodynamic stability in perovskite solar cells, especially by favoring high-iodide regions.
method: Graph neural network interatomic potentials were trained on DFT data to perform fast structure relaxations.
Secondary ML models predicted energies directly from unrelaxed structures.
The approach computed free-energy landscapes across compositions and phases while capturing disorder and FA orientations.
evidence_signal: The models were used to evaluate free-energy landscapes across the full composition space of (Cs/FA)Pb(Br/I)3 and (Cs/FA)Sn(Br/I)3, showing narrower stable regions for the Sn system and no stabilization near the center of composition space.
watch_item: Because the workflow relies on trained ML models, predictions should be validated carefully when extending to compositions, phases, or temperature regimes not well represented in the DFT training data.
paper_title: Charting the thermodynamic stability of hybrid perovskite alloys with machine learning
